name: Atomic Stage-Validate-Publish (WAP) for Data DAGs
tagline: Never write directly to live production partitions from retryable DAG tasks—always stage, validate invariants, and publish atomically.
purpose: Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) isolates unvalidated DAG outputs in a staging branch or prefix, runs automated data-quality gates, and promotes to production via an atomic metadata pointer swap.

spark.summary: Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) isolates unvalidated DAG outputs in a staging branch or prefix, runs automated data-quality gates, and promotes to production via an atomic metadata pointer swap.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep storage layouts predictable as data grows, never write directly to live production partitions from retryable DAG tasks—always stage, validate invariants, and publish atomically.
spark.byteSummary:
In Spark, Flink, and Airflow pipelines, writing directly to live production partitions exposes downstream consumers to partial writes, duplicate rows on task retries, and corrupt aggregations if a job fails halfway.

The **Stage-Validate-Publish (Write-Audit-Publish / WAP)** pattern writes all task outputs to an isolated staging prefix or Apache Iceberg branch (`_staging/run_id`). Once all tasks succeed, an automated validation gate checks row counts, null rates, and financial conservation laws (`sum(debits) == sum(credits)`).

Only after passing every gate does the orchestrator execute an O(1) atomic metadata commit (Iceberg `fast_forward` or Delta Lake transaction log commit) to make the new snapshot visible to readers.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Atomic Stage-Validate-Publish (WAP) for Data DAGs without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep storage layouts predictable as data grows, never write directly to live production partitions from retryable DAG tasks—always stage, validate invariants, and publish atomically.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Stage-Validate-Publish Orchestrator
learningJourney.purpose: Implement the WAP orchestrator so failed audits quarantine the branch and raise before touching production.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Stage-Validate-Publish Orchestrator** as the intuition layer for Atomic Stage-Validate-Publish (WAP) for Data DAGs: Implement the WAP orchestrator so failed audits quarantine the branch and raise before touching production.
explanation.core:
```python
def run_wap_pipeline(staging_writer, validator, catalog, run_id: str) -> str:
    branch = f'wap_{run_id}'
    staging_writer.write_to_branch(branch)
    metrics = validator.audit_branch(branch)
    if metrics['null_keys'] > 0 or metrics['net_imbalance'] != 0:
        catalog.tag_quarantine(branch)
        raise RuntimeError(f'WAP audit failed for {run_id}: {metrics}')
    snapshot_id = catalog.fast_forward_main(branch)
    return snapshot_id
```
